```{r}
#| label: early-session-setup
#| include: false

knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment = NA)

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(tidyverse))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(lubridate))

bca <- read_rds("Data/bca262.rds")

avg_price <- bca |>
  group_by(sale_year = year(sale_date)) |>
  summarise(avg_price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

avg_price_plot <- ggplot(avg_price, aes(sale_year, avg_price)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Average transaction price",
    caption = "2026: Jan–Feb only"
  )
```

## Install packages in the Console

Open Positron and run this once in the **Console**:

```r
install.packages("tidyverse")
```

### Console or R script?

Use the **Console**. Installation is a setup step, not a command that should run every time the analysis runs.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/03_Sample_Session.Rmd`.
:::

## Open the C407 folder as your workspace

Choose **File → Open Folder…** and select the **C407** folder.

Opening the folder:

- makes C407 the Positron workspace;
- sets R’s working directory to C407; and
- displays the course files in the Explorer.

::: {.key-point}
Open the folder itself—not `C407.Rproj`.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Positron workspaces and R project files: https://positron.posit.co/migrate-rstudio-rproj.html
:::

## Create the script and start clean

1. Create a new text file.
2. Save it as `Code/sample_session.R`.
3. Restart the active R interpreter with `Ctrl/Command + Shift + 0`.

Restarting removes objects created by earlier commands and gives the script a clean test environment.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/03_Sample_Session.Rmd`.
- Positron keyboard shortcuts: https://positron.posit.co/keyboard-shortcuts.html
:::

## Read the BCA sales data

Add this code to `sample_session.R`:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

bca <- read_rds("Data/bca262.rds")
dim(bca)
```

Run each statement with `Ctrl/Command + Enter`.

::: {.shortcut}
Insert `<-` with `Alt + -` on Windows/Linux or `Option + -` on macOS.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/03_Sample_Session.Rmd`.
- R shortcuts in Positron: https://positron.posit.co/guide-r.html
:::

## Browse the first six rows

Run this in the Console:

```r
bca |>
  head() |>
  View()
```

Positron opens the result in the **Data Explorer**.

::: {.shortcut}
Insert the pipe with `Ctrl + Shift + M` on Windows/Linux or `Command + Shift + M` on macOS.
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/03_Sample_Session.Rmd`.
- R shortcuts in Positron: https://positron.posit.co/guide-r.html
- Positron Data Explorer: https://positron.posit.co/data-explorer.html
:::

::: {.scroll-output}
```{r}
bca |>

```

Which columns might help explain differences in sale price?

## Check the two editing shortcuts

### What inserts the assignment operator `<-`?

### What inserts the pipe operator `|>`?

::: {.notes}
Answers:

- Assignment: `Alt + -` on Windows/Linux; `Option + -` on macOS.
- Pipe: `Ctrl + Shift + M` on Windows/Linux; `Command + Shift + M` on macOS.

[Sources]

- R shortcuts in Positron: https://positron.posit.co/guide-r.html
:::

## Calculate annual average prices

Add this code to the script:

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}
```r
library(lubridate)

avg_price <- bca |>
  group_by(sale_year = year(sale_date)) |>
  summarise(
    avg_price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```
:::

::: {.column width="41%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
avg_price |>
  tail(6)
```
:::
:::

Place the cursor anywhere in a complete statement and press `Ctrl/Command + Enter`.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/03_Sample_Session.Rmd`.
- Positron keyboard shortcuts: https://positron.posit.co/keyboard-shortcuts.html
:::

## Interpret the annual summary

```{r}
avg_price |>
  filter(sale_year %in% c(2000, 2010, 2024, 2025)) |>
  mutate(avg_price = scales::dollar(avg_price, accuracy = 1))
```

- The data begin in **2000**.
- The average rose by about **$575,343**, or **98.8%**, from 2010 to 2024.
- The 2026 observations cover only the available part of the year.

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course output: `../docs_2026/03_Sample_Session.html`.
:::

## Plot annual average prices

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="51%"}
```r
avg_price_plot <- ggplot(
  avg_price,
  aes(sale_year, avg_price)
) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_comma()
  ) +
  labs(
    caption = "2026: Jan–Feb only"
  )

avg_price_plot
```
:::

::: {.column width="47%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4.3
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of annual average BCA sale prices from 2000 through February 2026."

avg_price_plot
```
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Course source: `../docs_2026/03_Sample_Session.Rmd`.
:::

## Save the plot in the Temp folder

After creating the plot, run:

```r
ggsave(
  "Temp/avg_price.png",
  width = 8,
  height = 4.5
)
```

Use the Explorer to confirm that `avg_price.png` appears inside `C407/Temp`.

Save `Code/sample_session.R` before you finish.

::: {.key-point}
The script reproduces the analysis; the PNG carries the finished graph into documents and presentations.
:::
